title: Integrated communication: Public discourse — the long speech

frames.title: Lesson 114 · Integrated communication: Public discourse — the long speech

body: **Foco:** Comunicação integrada: Discurso público.
**Pronúncia:** Ritmo e ênfase para nuances.
**24 palavras novas** (discurso público).
**Texto do dia:** transcrição de palestra e podcast.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre o filibuster e a oratória maratona a partir da transcrição de um podcast, com ritmo e pausas bem marcados.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Podcast: “Words as Endurance”
paras: HOST: Today, the **filibuster**: the art of speaking **until the clock runs out**. In 1957, Senator Strom Thurmond **held the floor** for just over **twenty-four hours** against a civil-rights bill. **Reading** from, among other things, recipes and the Declaration of Independence, he **bought time** but **not the votes**; the bill **passed anyway**.

GUEST: What strikes me is that endurance **became the argument**. Nobody **quotes** what he said; they **remember** how long he said it. **That is the paradox**: a tactic **built on** words **empties** words of meaning.
GUEST: **Both**, and **that is why** it **divides** people. Supporters see **minority protection**; critics see **minority rule**.

items.q: Thurmond’s speech stopped the bill from passing.
The guest says endurance became the argument.
Everyone agrees the filibuster protects minorities.

blocks.body: No podcast, a fala usa **pseudo-cleft** (*What strikes me is…*) e **frases de ligação** para guiar o ouvinte. Faça pausa antes da ideia central.
*Filibuster* é substantivo e verbo: *He filibustered the bill.*

items.s: What ___ me is that endurance became the argument. (strike)
He ___ the floor for twenty-four hours. (hold, passado)
That is the ___: words empty words. (paradox)
Supporters see protection, ___ critics see rule by a minority. (while)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: What strikes you most about it
items.pt: O que mais lhe chama a atenção?
Que a resistência virou o argumento.

body: **Hold the floor** — manter a palavra
**Buy time** — ganhar tempo
**Run out the clock** — deixar o tempo se esgotar
**Talk the talk** — falar bonito
**Walk the walk** — cumprir o que diz
**Beat around the bush** — enrolar
**Dig in one’s heels** — empacar
**Stonewall** — obstruir
**Go the distance** — ir até o fim
**Filibuster a bill** — obstruir um projeto
**Was the filibuster rhetoric or obstruction?** — O filibuster era retórica ou obstrução?
**Both. That is why it divides people.** — Ambos. É por isso que divide as pessoas.
**What strikes you most about it?** — O que mais lhe chama a atenção?

forms: O senador obstruiu o projeto com um discurso longo.

blocks.title: Pronúncia: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.model: What strikes me is the length of the speech.
That is the paradox of the filibuster.
Supporters see protection, while critics see obstruction.

blocks.task: Write a 5-sentence podcast intro about a famous long speech, using What strikes me is…, That is the paradox and while.
blocks.model: Today we look at a speech that lasted over twenty-four hours. What strikes me is that nobody remembers a single line. That is the paradox of endurance as rhetoric. Supporters call it protection, while critics call it obstruction. Which is it? Let us find out.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
